newsitem.title: BOSNIA: OSCE says poll for new Bosnia going smoothly.
newsitem.headline: OSCE says poll for new Bosnia going smoothly.

text.p: Organisers of Bosnia's countrywide elections said on Saturday all routes across ethnic boundary lines were open and initial blockages had been cleared.

"Bosnia has unquestionably embarked on a democratic course, these elections are a crucial step in the continuing pursuit of a democratic voice," Agota Kuperman, a spokeswoman for the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), said.
Reading from a statement, Kuperman told reporters some 24 political parties and five coalitions were contesting the polls which she said were only a step on "the long road towards democratisation".

"We hope these elections will mark a start in bridging the ethnic divide created by four years of war," she said. The poll nine months after the Dayton peace accords would provide the institutions for a democratic, multi-ethnic state, she added.

Kuperman said the international community had succeeded in creating conditions in which the ballot could take place and OSCE expected large numbers of Bosnia's almost three million voters to exercise their right to vote.
"The conditions have been established, we no longer witness daily reports of killings and ethnic cleansing," she said.

She said OSCE, working closely with the NATO-led peace Implementation Force, had given the people of Bosnia "an opportunity to choose their future" and would remain in the country to monitor the results and human rights.
"OSCE is committed to Bosnia, our mandate has not come to an end with these elections, perhaps the most complex elections in history," she said.

Alex Ivanko, spokesman for the U.N. police task force, said reports that the road to Prijedor, in Serb northwest Bosnia, was blocked were not correct and a number of buses carrying Moslem refugees to vote had succeeded in crossing over the ethnic boundary line.
